description: PARSE_JSON / TRY_PARSE_JSON tolerate JSON strings that a strict parser rejects but Snowflake accepts. The SQL string-literal decode runs FIRST and consumes single backslashes, so a backslash-d reaches PARSE_JSON as plain d and keeping a regex backslash requires writing it doubled; an over-escaped quote likewise drops to a literal quote. Truly malformed JSON still errors under PARSE_JSON and yields NULL under TRY_PARSE_JSON. Snowflake's PARSE_JSON also accepts the non-standard JavaScript undefined token, which loaders guard against ingested artifacts with: a bare token in an ARRAY is the VARIANT undefined ELEMENT, so PARSE_JSON('[undefined]') renders [undefined] and EQUALS ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(NULL), which is what makes the guard fire, while in an OBJECT it degrades to a JSON null and the word inside a string value stays untouched. Converted 1:1 from functions/ParseJsonLenientTest (now retired); written through a generator using raw strings so the backslash forms survive both the JSON encoder and the testkit's own parser, and the assertNotNull checks become IFF(x IS NULL, ...) projections.

steps.sql: SELECT TRY_PARSE_JSON('{ not json at all')
SELECT PARSE_JSON('{ not json at all')

SELECT $1, PARSE_JSON($2), PARSE_JSON($2)
FROM VALUES
  ('alpha', '["widget one","node (a|p|m|q|f|fa|v)\d+","node \d+"]'),
  ('beta',  '["product two","(?<!skip )target"]'),
  ('gamma', '["foo\s*bar( baz)?","^alpha","^(?!.*x.*)(.*y.*)"]'),
  ('delta', '["first entry","second entry"]')

SELECT COUNT_IF(PARSE_JSON($2) IS NOT NULL) FROM VALUES
  ('alpha', '["widget one","node (a|p|m|q|f|fa|v)\d+","node \d+"]'),
  ('beta',  '["product two","(?<!skip )target"]'),
  ('gamma', '["foo\s*bar( baz)?","^alpha","^(?!.*x.*)(.*y.*)"]'),
  ('delta', '["first entry","second entry"]')
